title: Authenticated Observer Receipt Service
summary: P3E4 adds explicit producer enrollment, rootless workspace registration and atomic PostgreSQL ingestion of immutable Observer metadata. It returns durable replayable receipts without activating a publication or claiming remote source truth.
successor: Receipt/submission schemas and Server storage remain valid. P3E5 adds native Observer delivery and GET /api/v1/observer-identity; see shin-observer-delivery-v1. Versions and native-sender limitations in this document record the P3E4 receiver baseline.

sharedProtocol.dependencies: C++20, nlohmann JSON and OpenSSL Crypto only. No Core, filesystem, HTTP, PostgreSQL or runtime Observer dependency. Both Server and Observer use the same observation/submission validator.
sharedProtocol.submission: Existing shin.observer-submission.v1: exact envelope and payload fields, bounded positive sequences, slug identifiers, hexadecimal identities, SHA256 payload and submission identity, typed finite observation data. Compact envelope maximum is 8192 bytes. HTTP keeps its existing 32768-byte parse boundary and duplicate/depth rejection.
sharedProtocol.versions: Core and companion versions are independent and exposed honestly; linking unchanged Core dev.9 does not require inventing a Core release. No old schema reader is introduced.

workspaces.sourceKinds: local retains the immutable Server-authorized root and inode binding; observer has root/root_identity null and is bound only to explicit logical ids/source host. Git and a Server-local directory are not required for observer workspaces.
workspaces.POST /api/v1/projects/{project}/observer: Administrator, Idempotency-Key, exact body {id,display_name,source_host_id}. Registers source_kind=observer, never reads or creates a source directory. Returns workspace/replayed, 201 or 200. Existing local workspace registration remains explicit and restricted by allowed roots.
workspaces.localReporters: An administrator may also enroll an Observer for a known local workspace with the same registered source-host identity. source_kind describes Server filesystem visibility, not exclusive reporter eligibility. A producer report never changes source_kind, root, root identity or the independently verified Core route.
workspaces.routeBoundary: Native retrieval accepts only source_kind=local and its existing root/host/inode checks. Remote metadata cannot grant Server filesystem access, create a retrieval route or materialize an index.
workspaces.migration: Explicit SQL 007 preserves all schema 006 workspace bindings as local. It enriches old workspace registration response JSON with source_kind=local once, retaining other response fields and consumed request hashes. This is an intentional development response-shape upgrade, not byte-identical replay across versions or a dual runtime reader. Older SQL 001..006 checksums remain unchanged.

enrollment.POST /api/v1/observer-streams: Administrator; exact body {stream_id,project_id,workspace_id,principal_id,observer_id,source_host_id,profile,workspace_binding_digest}. HTTP requires a configured non-admin principal with explicit project access. Enrollment adds a narrowly scoped submission capability to that principal; an ordinary unenrolled reader cannot submit.
enrollment.binding: Stream identity is immutable. Registered workspace/source-host and all producer ids/profile/digest must match. One non-revoked stream per project/workspace/observer id prevents an implicit epoch replacement. Another stream requires explicit revocation/enrollment, never a clock-based takeover.
enrollment.replay: The same stream and canonical enrollment hash returns replayed=true plus current stored stream metadata. Changed binding conflicts. Replaying enrollment never clears revocation or restores permission.
enrollment.GET /api/v1/observer-streams/{stream}: Enrolled owner with current project access, or administrator. Returns bounded metadata/cursors/bytes only, not submission bodies or source. Other readers receive the same 404 as an absent stream.
enrollment.POST /api/v1/observer-streams/{stream}/r: Administrator and exact empty JSON body. Idempotently marks revoked and records audit in one transaction. Revocation blocks new submissions and replay POSTs; owner/admin may still inspect historical stream metadata.
enrollment.credentialBoundary: Bearer authentication uses existing private Server config. DB enrollment is additional per-stream authority, not a replacement for authentication or current project scope. Token configuration changes still require a deliberate Server restart; revocation itself is a live DB operation.

ingestion.POST /api/v1/observer-streams/{stream}/s: Exact shared submission envelope from the enrolled producer. No new Idempotency-Key is assigned: stream/sequence/submission_id are the operation identity. First committed acceptance returns 201/replayed=false; exact replay returns 200/replayed=true and the original receipt.
ingestion.transaction: Lock the stream row, validate owner/revocation/binding, look up replay, check order and capacity, reserve global quota, insert submission and receipt, advance accepted/observed cursors, append owner-scoped audit, then commit. A reply is produced only after commit. DB failure, including a failed audit insertion, rolls back the complete write unit.
ingestion.order: Accepted submission sequence must be exactly next. Same identity with different valid content is submission-conflict; missing/reversed order is observer-sequence-gap. Observation sequence must increase but may skip because local samples coalesce. A contiguous submission cursor does not prove that every source edit or observation was captured.
ingestion.receipt: shin.observer-ack.v1 has server_id, stream_id, sequence, submission_id, payload_sha256, project_id, workspace_id, received_at, verification_level=producer-observed, server_source_verified=false and shared_publication_mutated=false. Server identity is generated once in the DB singleton. Receipt and row use the same DB capture time; it is not a source freshness or commit-time guarantee.
ingestion.uncertainReply: A client with an ambiguous response must retry the identical retained submission, not assign a fresh identity. Revocation and current authorization are checked even on replay. The receipt is immutable DB evidence, not a standalone signed credential or permission to activate anything.
ingestion.auditPrivacy: Observer audit rows include stream/sequence foreign keys and are visible only to the enrolled owner or administrators, within normal project access. Enrollment audit actor may be the admin, but its visibility follows the stream owner. Ordinary project/workspace audit policy is unchanged.

limits.streams: 1024 retained streams globally and 128 per project. Revoked rows still consume history capacity.
limits.submissions: 1024 accepted receipts or 4MiB logical retained bytes per stream; 65536 receipts or 128MiB globally. Each submission plus receipt is at most 12288 compact serialized bytes. PostgreSQL row/index/storage overhead is not counted as payload bytes.
limits.concurrency: Short row transactions serialize one stream. Atomic quota-row updates prevent cross-stream over-admission. Shared audit advisory locking retains commit-order cursor semantics. Same-producer concurrency is not last-writer-wins.
limits.exhaustion: Explicit observer-capacity; no pruning, old receipt deletion, auto-disable or auto-activation. Exact authorized replay precedes quota checks. Server history retention is a separate required operational milestone before stable long-running use.

authority: Producer metadata remains producer-observed even when Server can also access a local workspace.
No source freshness, completeness, test execution, deployed state or project-wide readiness is inferred from an acknowledgement.
No ingestion path changes active_routes, preparations, source files, indexes, local outbox or commands.
Observer audit privacy is narrower than ordinary project/workspace registry metadata visibility.
deliveryBoundary: Server remains loopback-only with existing Host/Origin and Bearer guards. The integration harness explicitly transports native Observer records; Observer itself still has no network sender, acknowledgement import or queue drain. Authenticated endpoint/server-id binding, off-loopback TLS and safe local acknowledgement application must be implemented and verified before that next step. remote host networking, Desktop/tray and a separate Server UI are not delivered here.
